tex_content.label: gt.eq5.13
tex_content.html: \begin{equation} (\lambda I-T)x=y,\qquad (\lambda I-T^*)x=y \end{equation} have unique solutions and bounded inverses. For $\lambda \in \Lambda $, the two kernels are finite-dimensional and the respective equations are solvable exactly when $y$ is orthogonal to the kernel of the adjoint operator.
